market_name: Will 9 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether 2y/10y Treasury yields are falling and fed funds futures (SOFR/SR3) are pricing additional 2026 cuts; confirm the Polymarket move isn't a thin-liquidity blip.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT move vs rate-futures-implied easing; look for any Fed headline, economic data release, or crisis news that would justify a 9-cut repricing.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether risk-off (equities down, VIX up, credit spreads wider) accompanies the bond rally, confirming a recession/easing narrative vs a false signal.
time_plan.6h: Verify durability: has the Polymarket probability held, and are rate expectations across the curve consistent? Fade if reverting.
time_plan.12h: Final check at window close; mark whether TLT held its move and whether broader rates markets corroborated the signal.

predictions.reasoning: A 9-cut (225bps) scenario in 2026 is a deep-easing/recession tail. If this market's implied probability spikes sharply, it signals expectations of aggressive Fed easing — possibly emergency cuts. Long-duration Treasuries rally hard when the market prices rapid rate cuts, so TLT would rise. The move is directionally robust but a single Polymarket tail-strike shift is a noisy sensor and front-month Treasury reactions are driven primarily by official data/Fed speak, so 12h magnitude is modest.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY/EURUSD reaction and whether 2y yields fell; confirm rate-differential channel is dominating over safe-haven flows.
time_plan.1h: Watch for risk-off haven bid into USD that could offset the easing-driven weakness.
time_plan.2h: Assess cross-asset consistency: if gold is up and real yields down with USD weak, the easing thesis holds.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether USD move persists or reverses on haven demand.
time_plan.12h: Final assessment at close; note whether the dollar channel was dominated by easing or risk-off.

predictions.reasoning: Aggressive Fed easing expectations narrow US rate differentials and typically weaken the dollar, so a spike in the probability of 9 cuts would pressure the USD lower, benefiting UUP shorts. However, a tail recession scenario can also trigger safe-haven dollar demand, muddying the direction — hence lower confidence and a wide interval straddling zero.

evidence_used: Market question implies 9 cuts (~225bps) in 2026, an extreme deep-easing tail scenario
Resolution tied to FOMC statements and official fed funds target changes
Inclusion of emergency inter-meeting cuts signals a crisis/recession pathway
Standard rate-cut transmission: lower rates lift long bonds, pressure the dollar, support gold
uncertainty_notes: Polymarket tail-strike probabilities are thinly traded and noisy; a 'sharp move' may be liquidity-driven not information-driven
9 cuts is a far-tail event; small absolute probability changes can look large in percent terms without real information
Direction of USD is ambiguous because recession tails can trigger safe-haven dollar strength
12h window is too short for broad macro proxies to move 700bps; unlikely to be 'tradable' by the stated threshold
Mislabeled primary topic (military_conflict) suggests metadata noise

llm_justification.summary: This market prices an extreme deep-easing scenario (nine 25bps Fed cuts in 2026). A sharp rise in its implied probability would signal expectations of aggressive Fed easing, likely tied to recession or crisis. The cleanest public-market reads are long-duration Treasuries higher (TLT up) and the dollar lower (UUP down), though the dollar's direction is complicated by potential safe-haven flows. Given the noisiness of a far-tail Polymarket strike and a 12h window, moves are unlikely to reach the 700bps tradable threshold; this is a directional research mapping with moderate-to-low confidence.
key_assumptions: A sharp probability move reflects genuine easing/recession repricing, not thin-market noise
Standard monetary transmission holds: more expected cuts lift bonds and weaken USD
The move in the prediction market is roughly contemporaneous with, not lagging, rates markets
failure_modes: The Polymarket shift is already reflected in SOFR futures and Treasuries — no leak, no edge
Thin liquidity on a far-tail strike produces a fake signal that reverts within hours
Recession-driven safe-haven demand lifts the dollar instead of weakening it, breaking the UUP thesis
Broad ETF proxies simply do not move 700bps in 12h, so nothing is tradable under the threshold
The easing narrative is offset by inflation concerns keeping long yields elevated despite cut expectations
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
